description:
Find and remove dead, stale and duplicated CODE, so the tree is what it claims to be.

RUN THIS LAST, DELIBERATELY. It carries a high number because a cleanup that runs before the work is finished deletes scaffolding that was about to be used, and then the next tasklist re-adds it. The roadmap should be substantially complete before this executes.

WHAT COUNTS AS DEAD. Unreferenced modules, functions and files; duplicated implementations of one behaviour; code behind flags that can no longer be set; scripts nothing runs; dependencies nothing imports; commented-out blocks kept 'just in case'. What does NOT count: code a test exercises, code an external consumer calls, and code that is deliberately unexercised and says so.

THE STANDARD OF PROOF, AND IT IS THE WHOLE TASKLIST. This portfolio has repeatedly found things that LOOKED dead and were not — a Prolog corpus reached by a path nobody found, `content_qa` declared callerless when it had a caller, `docs/studioos` cited by 93 files. Deletion is irreversible in effect even when git remembers, because nobody re-reads a deleted file. Every removal names the search that found nothing.

PAIRED WITH THE DOCS SWEEP, WHICH RUNS AFTER. Removing code changes what the docs should say, so the docs tasklist depends on this one. Do not fix docs here beyond what a removal strands.

userStories.title: An inventory, measured before anything is removed
userStories.notes: Inventory shipped as docs/explanation/dead-code-audit.md, linked from docs/README.md. Every candidate names its search command and scope. Measured: 560 production shell functions scanned, exactly 1 with zero references (crossrepo_completed, engine/crossrepo.sh:33); 98 single-call-site (excluded as a decomposition metric, not liveness); 142 CHIEF_* identifiers scanned, 3 write-only; 12 duplicate definitions found and ALL 12 classified as deliberate degradation stubs (Class B, do not remove); 3 test files in zero gate lists; 1 script invoked by nothing; 0 commented-out blocks; 0 unreferenced docs/templates/fixtures. Genuinely-dead (Class A) and deliberately-unexercised (Class B) are separate sections, and Section 5 records 11 candidates that looked dead and are live, with why. Gate: chief verify exit 0, GREEN — path-scoped to the changed paths (docs + tasklists): doc-links 0 dead vs 0 on main, tasklists jq parse OK; verdict RECORDED for tree 45c5aafe. chief lint: 4 tasklists clean. quality ratchet: no code diff vs main.
acceptanceCriteria: Produce a checked-in inventory of candidates with, for each, the SEARCH that found it unreferenced — the command and its scope. A candidate list without its method is unreviewable, and this is the artifact a human approves before deletion.
Separate genuinely-dead from deliberately-unexercised. The second class exists here on purpose (refusal paths, guards, unreached tiers that say so) and deleting it removes a stated contract.
Include duplicated implementations as first-class findings, not just unused ones — two implementations of one behaviour is the failure mode that costs most later, because they drift.
GATES: the repo's own verify green.

userStories.title: Removal, with the tree still green and the reason recorded
userStories.notes: Three reviewable commits + one separate pre-existing fix; disposition of every US-1 finding in docs/explanation/dead-code-audit.md §8, with §§2-5 left AS MEASURED. RULE APPLIED: unreferenced code is deleted, working code that no gate invokes is REGISTERED — a test in zero gate lists is worse than an absent one because it reads as coverage. REMOVED (2 of 6 findings, step 1/3 2c5ee09): crossrepo_completed() (engine/crossrepo.sh — the only zero-reference function of 560; header amended so the SET/PRINT pair rule does not read as a claim of symmetry) and CHIEF_SWEEP_STARTUP_BYTES/_COUNT (engine/sweep.sh — 1 tree-wide hit each, and it is the write); both searches re-run immediately before deletion and pasted into the commit. REGISTERED (4, step 2/3 e9738e5): parked-decisions + update-reroot into all three gate lists, ps-all into BASH_SUITE + CI only (real watcher, monitor.sh's exclusion, stated in its header), check-tasklist-categories.mjs into .chief/verify.sh + CI. NOT REMOVED, recorded with why (§8.3): all 12 duplicate definitions (degradation stubs — deleting them leaves every test green and removes the compatibility story), CHIEF_SWEEP_REFUSED (declared an output at sweep.sh:187), the 98 single-call-site functions, every row of §5, engine/reap.sh:14. MEASURED: parked-decisions PASS 0.36s; update-reroot PASS 5.6s; ps-all was RED 3/3 (fixed 0.2s sleep vs a ~400ms first render) and is PASS 3/3 after waiting for the render; categories guard 'OK — 4 tasklists categorized'; both new merge-gate entries PASS under test/bystander.sh (2/2, bystander alive); doc-links 0 dead vs 0 on main; doc-sync PASS 42 merged tasklists; version-bump PASS 0.9.14; crossrepo XREPO PASS; sweep 55 passed 0 failed. Also fixed, separately: ROADMAP had never named 118 (main is red on doc-sync today), and CI HAD NOT PARSED SINCE 2026-08-25 — five step names beginning with a backtick, a reserved YAML indicator; run 33047688561 is a run of the FILE with jobs=[]. Quoted; the file now parses, 72 steps. GATE: chief verify exit 0, GREEN, ~20 min: quality ratchet OK; bash -n clean; version-bump PASS (0.9.14); bystander block 57 test(s) (55 before this branch, +2 for the new registrations) with the decoy run alive and a genuine orphan still reaped; doc-sync PASS (v0.9.14, 42 merged tasklists); tasklists jq parse + category coverage OK; verdict RECORDED for tree fb83c89c
acceptanceCriteria: Remove what US-1 established, in reviewable steps rather than one sweep. A single commit deleting hundreds of lines across unrelated subsystems cannot be reviewed and cannot be partially reverted.
The full gate passes after each step. A removal that needs a test deleted to stay green is a removal of something live — say so and stop rather than adjusting the test.
Anything NOT removed that looked dead is recorded with why it survived. That record is worth more than the deletions: it is what stops the next sweep re-litigating the same files.
GATES: the repo's own verify green.

userStories.title: What the sweep could not decide
acceptanceCriteria: Report candidates the sweep could not resolve — reachable only through dynamic dispatch, reflection, generated code, or a consumer outside this repo — and leave them in place. An honest 'undecidable' list is a legitimate result.
State the limits of the method: what a static search over this tree cannot see. Cross-repo consumers are the obvious one, and this portfolio has already been bitten by exactly that.
GATES: the repo's own verify green.
